title: Encrypted volume table
whyItMatters: crypttab names the encrypted volumes unlocked at boot and how they are keyed. It tells a buyer which disks are protected and whether a key file on the disk was used.
source: crypttab(5) manual page: /etc/crypttab describes encrypted block devices unlocked at boot: https://man.archlinux.org/man/crypttab.5
notes: Entries name the backing device, the mapping name, the key file or none, and options. No key material is stored here. Full-disk encryption set up by the installer is usually not listed, so an absent file does not mean the disk is unencrypted. Where /etc is unreadable the engine records a permission skip.

cleanup.risk: The file stays until a reinstall; editing or deleting it by hand can stop the machine booting, so leave it alone.
cleanup.reason: This system configuration file maps encrypted block devices at boot time and will be cleared upon OS reinstallation.
